title: Lam Sơn uprising against Ming rule
summary: From 1418 the landowner Lê Lợi led a ten-year armed resistance, centred on his home district of Lam Sơn in Thanh Hóa, against Ming occupation of Vietnam. His early campaigns often failed, but by 1425 he was winning repeatedly, and in 1428 he proclaimed himself emperor and began the Lê dynasty.

uncertainty.note: Start: the Vietnam National Museum of History says Lê Lợi formally raised the banner of the Lam Sơn uprising in 1418, while EBSCO says the resistance was officially declared in 1417. End: the museum dates the ten-year resistance 1418-1427; EBSCO dates Lê Lợi proclaiming himself emperor to 1428.
